stem: How will you convert ethanoic acid into benzene?
solution:
\(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH(aq)}} \text{CH}_3\text{COONa} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{Soda lime}} \text{CH}_4 \xrightarrow[h\nu]{\text{Cl}_2} \text{CH}_3\text{Cl}\)

\(\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[\text{Wurtz reaction}]{\text{Na/dry ether}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{Cl}_2} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}} \text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2\)

\(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2} \text{CH}_2\text{Br}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}} \text{CH}_2=\text{CHBr} \xrightarrow{\text{NaNH}_2} \text{CH}\equiv\text{CH}\)

\(3\,\text{CH}\equiv\text{CH} \xrightarrow[873\,\text{K}]{\text{Red hot iron tube}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_6\) (benzene)

stem: How do you account for the formation of ethane during chlorination of methane?

Write IUPAC names of the following compounds :

(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2\)

(b) \(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3\)

(c) the bond-line structure shown in the figure

(d) a benzene ring bearing the chain \(-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2\)

(e) a benzene ring bearing a \(-\text{CH}_3\) group and, on the adjacent ring carbon, an \(-\text{OH}\) group

(f) \(\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_4\,\text{CH}\,(\text{CH}_2)_3\,\text{CH}_3\) with \(-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2\) attached to the central CH

(g) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2\)
_note: Sub-items (c), (d) and (e) are printed as drawn structures. (d) and (e) are stated in words here because they are unambiguous; (c) is a bare bond-line drawing and is carried as a figure so the question stays answerable without describing it.
